correctness.rationale: A support face contains at most one vertex in each column, so no nonidentity color translation can preserve a nonempty support. The first-column closed stars are cones and cover the complex. Pairwise intersections omit column one and exclude two colors from column two. For m=3,q≥4, the allowed column-two vertices share neighbors in column three (two such vertices exclude at most two colors), and every column-three vertex has an allowed neighbor. For m≥4 all allowed column-two vertices connect to all column-four vertices; every column-three vertex joins to a different color in column four, and each later column joins to column two. All these pairwise intersections share a fixed column-three vertex, so each successive attachment to the union is along a connected subcomplex. Subcomplex van Kampen (or edge paths through the common vertex) proves simple connectivity. The free finite action then gives the universal cover and fundamental group C_q. For m=1 the quotient is a point; for m=2 it has two vertices and q−1 parallel edges. For m=q=3 each triangle with distinct endpoint colors uniquely uses its nonconsecutive opposite edge, so the first free-face collapse works in entire orbits. After those collapses, the remaining triangles have equal endpoint colors and each has a unique free 1–2 edge. The resulting hexagon plus three leaves descends to a connected three-vertex three-edge graph. This proves the exceptional quotient group, not just its abelianization. The same freeness argument works for a free diagonal action of a finite group on its color set.
residual_risks: Finite exact homology checks, if replayed, check quotient chain signs and abelianizations, not universal covers or π₁ itself. The proof controls the actual geometric quotient and does not extend to nonfree actions.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct content is the general-q threshold at q≥4 for simple connectivity and the resulting sharp cyclic quotient classification with unbounded torsion orders. Thapper's older triangular-cylinder theorem already gives the simply connected q=3 regime, and with freeness implies the C₃ quotient there; that case is not credited as new. The same-day triangular torsion record actually uses this implication and mentions a broader determination without identifying a separate complete source. Its actual theorem does not cover q≥4. The small graph cases and covering-space mechanism are standard rather than independent contributions.
residual_risks: No global priority guarantee for q≥4; an unindexed connectivity result may exist. The same-day triangular record's mention of a broader determination does not resolve chronology or identify an independent exact match.
